Sensitivity Analysis for the Power of a Targeted Regression Coefficient

Source: R/ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity.R
ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity.Rd

Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis for the statistical power of the t-test of a targeted regression coefficient. Given a planned (supposed_*) covariance structure and a true (true_*) covariance structure, the function draws G replications, fits the multiple regression, and reports the empirical proportion of replications on which the t-test of the targeted coefficient rejects, together with the realized distribution of the estimated unstandardized coefficient \(\hat b_j\), its standard error, and the test statistic. ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity() is the power-oriented sibling of ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity (which is CI-width oriented).

Usage

ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity(
  true_var_Y = NULL,
  true_cov_YX = NULL,
  true_cov_XX = NULL,
  supposed_var_Y = NULL,
  supposed_cov_YX = NULL,
  supposed_cov_XX = NULL,
  specified_N = NULL,
  which_predictor = 1,
  desired_power = 0.85,
  alpha_level = 0.05,
  directional = FALSE,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = TRUE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_var_Y

Population variance of the dependent variable (Y)

true_cov_YX

Population covariance vector between the p predictor variables and the dependent variable (Y)

true_cov_XX

Population covariance matrix of the p predictor variables

supposed_var_Y

Supposed variance of the dependent variable (Y), the planning value used in sample size planning. Defaults to true_var_Y.

supposed_cov_YX

Supposed covariance vector between the predictor variables and the dependent variable, the planning values used in sample size planning. Defaults to true_cov_YX.

supposed_cov_XX

Supposed covariance matrix of the predictor variables, the planning values used in sample size planning. Defaults to true_cov_XX.

specified_N

Directly specified sample size; if supplied, sample size planning is skipped.

which_predictor

Index identifying which of the p predictors is the targeted predictor for the power test.

desired_power

Desired degree of statistical power used for planning

alpha_level

Type I error rate

directional

Whether a one-sided or two-sided test is used

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications

print_iter

Whether to print the iteration number during the simulation

filename

Optional path of a CSV file to receive the per-replication results (the coefficient estimate reg_coef_j, its standard error se_reg_coef_j, the t statistic t_value, and the observed \(R^2\) R2), overwriting any file already at that path; the default NULL writes nothing, and a throwaway run that wants the file should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value summarizing the Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis. The term entries are: total_N (the sample size evaluated), empirical_power, analytic_power (computed from ss_power_reg_coef), the mean / median / SD of the realized \(\hat b_j\) (mean_reg_coef_j, median_reg_coef_j, sd_reg_coef_j), of its standard error (mean_se_reg_coef_j, median_se_reg_coef_j, sd_se_reg_coef_j), of the test statistic (mean_t_value, median_t_value, sd_t_value), and of the squared multiple correlation coefficient (mean_R2, median_R2, sd_R2), t_crit (the critical value), and the input echoes p, which_predictor, true_reg_coef_j and supposed_reg_coef_j (the population and planning values of the targeted coefficient implied by the supplied covariance structures), desired_power (NA when specified_N was supplied instead), and alpha_level. The result carries the dmar_ss_power_sensitivity class, so tidy reports the planned sample size beside the empirical and analytic power, and glance adds the simulated estimator distribution beside the echoed inputs.

Details

When the supposed and true covariance structures are identical, the function performs a Monte Carlo evaluation of the planning procedure (no misspecification); when they differ, it performs a sensitivity analysis on the consequences of misspecifying the population covariance structure for the targeted coefficient's power. The planning step calls ss_power_reg_coef with the supposed covariance structure; the simulation step generates data from the true covariance structure.

The coefficient is the unstandardized one, \(b_j\), the jth element of \(\Sigma_{XX}^{-1}\sigma_{XY}\), from true_cov_XX and true_cov_YX for the true value and from their supposed counterparts for the supposed value, and every replication is fit in the units of the data. The t statistic of a coefficient is the same whether or not the data are standardized, so the power is that of the test of the standardized coefficient as well; the standardized coefficient itself, \(b_j \sigma_{X_j}/\sigma_Y\) (Kelley & Maxwell, 2003, p. 316), and its precision are the subject of ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical power analysis for the behavioral sciences (2nd ed.). Hillsdale, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum.

Kelley, K., & Maxwell, S. E. (2003). Sample size for multiple regression: Obtaining regression coefficients that are accurate, not simply significant. Psychological Methods, 8(3), 305–321. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.8.3.305

Kelley, K., & Maxwell, S. E. (2008). Sample size planning with applications to multiple regression: Power and accuracy for omnibus and targeted effects. In P. Alasuutari, L. Bickman, & J. Brannen (Eds.), The Sage handbook of social research methods (pp. 166–192). Sage.

Maxwell, S. E. (2000). Sample size and multiple regression analysis. Psychological Methods, 5(4), 434–458. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.5.4.434

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapter 4 on individual comparisons of means and Chapter 6 on trend analysis.)

Examples

# Targeted coefficient power sensitivity with two predictors. The
# default G = 1000 replications is used in practice; G is reduced here
# so the example runs quickly.
set.seed(113)
cov_XX  <- matrix(c(1, 0.3, 0.3, 1), nrow = 2)
cov_YX  <- c(0.4, 0.3)
ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity(
  true_var_Y = 1, true_cov_YX = cov_YX, true_cov_XX = cov_XX,
  which_predictor = 1, desired_power = 0.80,
  G = 100, print_iter = FALSE
)
#>  term                 value
#>  total_N              62   
#>  empirical_power      0.800
#>  analytic_power       0.801
#>  mean_reg_coef_j      0.351
#>  median_reg_coef_j    0.347
#>  sd_reg_coef_j        0.120
#>  mean_se_reg_coef_j   0.120
#>  median_se_reg_coef_j 0.119
#>  sd_se_reg_coef_j     0.016
#>  mean_t_value         2.939
#>  median_t_value       3.001
#>  sd_t_value           1.019
#>  mean_R2              0.222
#>  median_R2            0.210
#>  sd_R2                0.085
#>  t_crit               2.001
#>  p                    2    
#>  which_predictor      1    
#>  true_reg_coef_j      0.341
